editorial:
Imagine spending a whole week with a guy who has absolutely nothing going for him. That is exactly what you get with Ripa, a long-haired mess of a human who spends more time drinking than sleeping. He thinks he is a great filmmaker, but his past movies were way too gross and violent for anyone to actually like. You will see him drifting from bar to bar, barely remembering where he was the night before, just trying to survive his own bad choices. The vibe is gritty and messy, but it is also funny because Ripa is such a disaster of a person.

You will probably love how honest the acting feels, as it captures that feeling of being stuck in a rut perfectly. The pacing is a bit slow in spots, but meeting Tiina, the bank teller, adds a nice spark to the story. It is a great pick if you like stories about losers who might actually have a heart. If you want to check it out, try renting it on Apple TV for a quick watch, or if you are a fan of old-school cinema, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: By the end, you see that Ripa is still mostly the same old mess, but meeting Tiina gives him a tiny bit of hope. He does not suddenly become a millionaire or a famous director, which keeps the story real. He finally faces the fact that his life is a wreck, but he finds a small amount of peace. It wraps up by showing that even someone as lost as Ripa can find a human connection.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves character studies about messy people and indie comedies.
